newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to hold special parliament from Nov 7 -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to hold special parliament from Nov 7 -- MOF.

text.p: Japan's cabinet has formally decided to hold a special session of parliament for six days from November 7 to name the next prime minister, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told a news conference on Friday.
Kubo added that if new government decided to hold an extraordinary session of parliament after the special session, it would likely start in late November or early December.
Kubo said that if there was an extraordinary session, a special committee would likely conduct a review of Japan's tax system in the light of a planned increase in the consumption tax from April 1.
He reiterated that the government would not change its plan to increase the tax from the current three percent to five percent.

Kubo said the next fiscal year's state budget was being drafted on the premise that the consumption tax was going to be increased. He said he believed the special committee would hold "realistic" discussions in reviewing the consumption tax.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party, the Social Democratic Party and the Sakigake Party formed a new political alliance on Thursday, in which they agreed to set up a special parliamentary committee in the next extraordinary session to review the tax system.
They also agreed to set up a body to oversee financial institutions seperate from the Finance Ministry and to seek to strengthen the independence of the Bank of Japan.
MOF will respect the agreement reached by the parties on reforms, but Kubo said it was important for the ministry to be able to voice its opinions on the reforms.
There were still issues to be settled in separating the body to oversee financial institutions, such as who will be responsible for the body and what to do about regional networks, Kubo said.
